summary: Phase 5 of 6. Builds the full Streamlit dashboard suite on top of the Phase 4 spend cube and diagnostics. Implements: shared components (charts, filters, tables), dashboard app shell with navigation, spend overview page, category deep dive, supplier deep dive, payment terms deep dive, and data quality page. Validation gate: all 5 dashboard pages render with test data, filters work, drill-downs function.

decisions.data_loading: Dashboard loads from data/output/transactions.parquet (built by Phase 4). Falls back to loading from SQLite if Parquet not found. Uses st.cache_data for all data loads.
decisions.shared_filters: Global filter sidebar in dashboard/components/filters.py — date range, business unit, category L1, supplier — applied consistently across all pages via session_state.
decisions.chart_library: Plotly Express for all charts (already in requirements.txt). No Altair, no Matplotlib.
decisions.page_structure: Streamlit multipage app — dashboard/app.py is the entry point with navigation. Pages in dashboard/pages/ follow Streamlit naming convention (01_spend_overview.py etc.).
decisions.kpi_cards: KPI cards implemented as st.metric() components arranged in st.columns(). Consistent styling across all pages.
decisions.no_auth: Single-user local app — no authentication layer per spec.
decisions.phase_foundation: Phase 4 complete. data/output/transactions.parquet, by_supplier.parquet, by_category.parquet, by_month.parquet exist. CubeMetrics and DataQualityDiagnostics importable from src/.

key_files: dashboard/app.py - placeholder, implement as Streamlit entry point
dashboard/components/charts.py - placeholder, implement reusable chart functions
dashboard/components/filters.py - placeholder, implement shared filter sidebar
dashboard/components/tables.py - placeholder, implement reusable table components
patterns_to_follow: Shared filters in st.sidebar via dashboard/components/filters.py
All monetary values formatted as f'{value:,.0f} AUD' or similar
Plotly figures use consistent colour palette
Each page is self-contained — imports from src/ for data access
st.set_page_config called in app.py only (not individual pages)

userStories.title: Implement shared dashboard components
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/components/ — the shared building blocks used by all dashboard pages: reusable chart functions, filter sidebar, and table components.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/components/filters.py — implement render_filters(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: renders st.sidebar with date range picker (invoice_date), business unit multiselect, category L1 multiselect, supplier search text input. Returns filtered DataFrame. Uses st.session_state to persist filter values.

Edit file: dashboard/components/charts.py — implement these functions using plotly.express: bar_chart(df, x, y, title, color=None) -> go.Figure; horizontal_bar(df, x, y, title, max_rows=20) -> go.Figure; treemap(df, path, values, title) -> go.Figure; line_chart(df, x, y, title) -> go.Figure; donut_chart(df, names, values, title) -> go.Figure; pareto_chart(df, x, y, title) -> go.Figure (bar + cumulative % line on secondary y-axis); heatmap(df, x, y, values, title) -> go.Figure. All figures use consistent layout: white background, no gridlines on y-axis, font_size=12.

Edit file: dashboard/components/tables.py — implement: styled_dataframe(df, format_cols: dict = None) -> None: calls st.dataframe with column formatting. format_monetary(df, cols: list) -> pd.DataFrame: formats monetary columns as '{:,.0f}'. kpi_row(metrics: dict) -> None: renders a row of st.metric() cards from a dict of {label: (value, delta_optional)}.
Verify: python -c 'from dashboard.components import charts, filters, tables; print("Components OK")' — exits 0

userStories.title: Implement dashboard app shell and data loader
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/app.py as the Streamlit entry point with page navigation and a shared data loading function used by all pages.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/app.py — implement the main Streamlit app entry point
Set page config: st.set_page_config(page_title='SpendCube', page_icon='💰', layout='wide', initial_sidebar_state='expanded')

Implement load_cube_data() -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame] decorated with @st.cache_data: loads transactions.parquet, by_supplier.parquet, by_category.parquet, by_month.parquet from data/output/. If any Parquet not found, shows st.error with instructions to run make build-cube.
Implement load_quality_scorecard() -> dict decorated with @st.cache_data: loads data/output/quality_scorecard.json. Returns empty dict if not found.
Home page content: title 'SpendCube — Procurement Analytics', brief description, quick stats (total spend, supplier count, invoice count) if data available, link to run pipeline if no data found.
Import and expose load_cube_data and load_quality_scorecard for use by page modules.
Run: streamlit run dashboard/app.py --server.headless true -- 2>&1 | head -5 — should start without import errors (may show 'You can now view...' or similar)

userStories.title: Implement spend overview dashboard page
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/pages/01_spend_overview.py — the main high-level spend overview page with KPI cards, spend trends, category breakdown, top suppliers, and Pareto curve.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/01_spend_overview.py — implement full spend overview page
Row 1 — KPI cards (st.columns(6)): Total Spend (AUD), Supplier Count, Invoice Count, Avg Transaction Size, Contract Coverage %, Tail Spend %
Row 2 — Spend by month (bar chart, full width): x=invoice_month, y=sum(base_amount). Add 3-month rolling average trend line.
Row 3 left — Spend by category L1 (horizontal bar, top 10). Row 3 right — Spend by business unit (horizontal bar).
Row 4 — Top 20 suppliers (horizontal bar with canonical_supplier_name). Overlay cumulative spend % as secondary line.

Row 5 left — Pareto curve (supplier rank vs cumulative % spend). Row 5 right — Direct vs Indirect split donut (spend_type) OR Managed vs Unmanaged donut (managed_status). Use whichever has more non-null data.
Row 6 — Data quality scorecard mini-view: show 9 check statuses as coloured badges.
Apply filters from render_filters() in sidebar. All charts update when filters change.
Page title: 'Spend Overview'

userStories.title: Implement category deep dive page
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/pages/02_category_deep_dive.py — drill-down from L1 to L2 to L3 category with spend trends, supplier fragmentation, and savings lever flags.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/02_category_deep_dive.py — implement category deep dive page
Category selector: st.selectbox for L1 → st.selectbox for L2 (filtered by L1) → st.selectbox for L3 (filtered by L2). Show 'All' option at each level.
KPI row for selected category: Total Spend, Supplier Count, Invoice Count, Contract Coverage %, Maverick Spend %, Avg Payment Terms
Spend trend: monthly spend bar chart for selected category
Top suppliers in category: horizontal bar (top 10 by spend)
Supplier fragmentation: show supplier count, HHI for category, top-1 supplier share %
Payment terms distribution: histogram of payment_terms_days for transactions in category

Savings lever flags panel: show applicable flags as st.info() boxes — e.g. if supplier_count > 5: 'Consolidation opportunity: {n} suppliers', if maverick_pct > 15%: 'High maverick spend ({pct}%)', if avg_terms < 30: 'Short payment terms opportunity'
Page title: 'Category Deep Dive'

userStories.title: Implement supplier deep dive page
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/pages/03_supplier_deep_dive.py — supplier search and drill-down with spend breakdown, related entities, and payment terms.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/03_supplier_deep_dive.py — implement supplier deep dive page
Supplier selector: st.selectbox with list of canonical_supplier_names sorted by spend desc. Show spend next to name: 'Telstra Corporation (AUD 22,500)'.
KPI row: Total Spend, Invoice Count, Avg Transaction Size, Payment Terms (days), Contract Coverage %
Spend trend: monthly spend for selected supplier
Spend by category: horizontal bar (top categories for this supplier)
Spend by business unit / site: horizontal bar
Related entities panel: show other suppliers with same parent_company_name (if any), show suppliers with similar names (fuzzy matches from supplier_match_log with review_status=PENDING)

Risk flags: if supplier_spend / total_spend > 0.20: 'High concentration: {pct}% of total spend', if is_single_category (all spend in one L1): 'Single source risk', if contract_coverage < 0.5: 'Low contract coverage'
Page title: 'Supplier Deep Dive'

userStories.title: Implement payment terms deep dive page
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/pages/04_payment_terms.py — weighted average payment terms analysis with working capital opportunity sizing and renegotiation priority list.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/04_payment_terms.py — implement payment terms page
KPI row: Weighted Avg Payment Terms (days), % Transactions with Terms, Working Capital Opportunity (AUD, at target 45 days, WACC 8%), # Suppliers on Short Terms (<30 days)
Distribution histogram: payment_terms_days distribution across all transactions (plotly histogram, bin size 5 days)
Heatmap: top 15 suppliers × payment terms bucket (0-14, 15-30, 31-45, 46-60, 60+) — colour = spend

Working capital table: for each supplier with terms < config target (45 days), show: Supplier, Current Terms, Target Terms, Annual Spend, WC Opportunity (AUD). Sorted by WC Opportunity desc. Formula: (target - current) / 365 * annual_spend * wacc.
Non-standard terms: show suppliers with payment_terms_days not in (14, 30, 45, 60, 90) as anomaly list
st.number_input for target payment days (default 45) and WACC % (default 8) — recalculates WC opportunity dynamically
Page title: 'Payment Terms'

userStories.title: Implement data quality dashboard page
userStories.description: Implement dashboard/pages/05_data_quality.py — the data quality scorecard page showing all 9 diagnostic checks with drill-down into problematic records.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/05_data_quality.py — implement data quality page
Overall quality score: st.metric('Overall Data Quality', f'{score}/100') as a large header metric

Scorecard table: st.dataframe showing all 9 checks with columns: Check, Value, Status (coloured), Green Threshold, Amber Threshold, Remediation. Use pandas Styler to colour Status column (green/amber/red).

Drill-down expandable sections (st.expander) for each RED or AMBER check: show the actual problematic rows. E.g. for 'Missing supplier name': show transactions where raw_supplier_name is null. For 'Duplicate invoice risk': show the duplicate invoice pairs.
Export button: st.download_button to download quality_scorecard.json
Refresh button: st.button('Re-run diagnostics') — clears st.cache_data and reloads
Page title: 'Data Quality'

userStories.title: Update Makefile serve target and validate all pages render
userStories.description: Ensure make serve-dashboard works, all 5 pages import cleanly, and validate the dashboard runs without errors on sample data.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: Makefile — update serve-dashboard target to: streamlit run dashboard/app.py

Validate all page imports: python -c 'import dashboard.pages.01_spend_overview' fails due to numeric prefix — use importlib instead. Instead verify: python -c 'import importlib.util; [importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(f, f"dashboard/pages/{f}") for f in ["01_spend_overview.py","02_category_deep_dive.py","03_supplier_deep_dive.py","04_payment_terms.py","05_data_quality.py"]]; print("All pages loadable")'
Verify no import errors: python -c 'from dashboard.components.charts import bar_chart, horizontal_bar, treemap, line_chart, donut_chart, pareto_chart, heatmap; print("Charts OK")'
Verify: python -c 'from dashboard.components.filters import render_filters; from dashboard.components.tables import kpi_row, styled_dataframe; print("Components OK")'
Verify: python -c 'from dashboard.app import load_cube_data, load_quality_scorecard; print("App loader OK")'

Run: streamlit run dashboard/app.py --server.headless true &> /tmp/streamlit_test.log & sleep 5 && kill %1 && grep -v 'Warning\|DeprecationWarning' /tmp/streamlit_test.log | head -10 — should show startup without Python errors
